scope: Read-only primary-source and manuscript proof comparison. No existing repository file was changed by this audit.

sources.title: Lonely Runner Relations
sections_read: Section 3: Proposition 3.1, Theorem 3.2, complete lattice-width proof
sources.comparison: For ordinary cover/tight instances, short integer relations constrain the velocity vector. The geometric argument computes translated-zonotope width and forces a relation orthogonal to the velocity vector. It gives no stated bound on each inserted velocity. A short relation may involve retained baseline speeds only. Translation drops out of width, so this criterion does not classify fixed-support local phase schedules. This is a comparison with the inspected statements and proofs, not a claim that their methods admit no further consequences.

sources.title: Linearly-exponential checking is enough for the Lonely Runner Conjecture and some of its variants
sections_read: Theorems A and B with all hypotheses
Section 2: short-vector and covering-radius projection tools
Section 3: projection mechanism and complete proof of Theorem A
Section 4.1: proof mechanism for Theorem B
sources.comparison: Theorem A assumes ordinary LRC in the preceding dimension and proves the standard non-strict lower bound for primitive vectors above a gcd-sum cutoff bounded by binomial(n+1,2)^(n-1). Theorem B additionally assumes shifted LRC in the preceding dimension and the Lonely Vector Property through size n. Projection can combine or delete generators and changes dimension; it does not preserve fixed runner labels and removal/rephasing/addition roles. These statements do not directly give an unconditional cubic bound for every two-entry cover, or the fixed-support local affinization theorem. Finite checking and zonotopal geometry are established methodological precedents.

relation_inference_countermodel.meaning: These vectors satisfy a short relation with odd coefficient sum for arbitrarily large inserted speeds. They are not asserted covers or tight instances. This refutes inference of an insertion bound from the necessary short-relation condition alone.

manuscript_review.theorem_5: No quantifier loss found. Supports are finite and fixed; locality at scale one along an unbounded sequence suffices. One joint torus subsequence and one joint extended-real subsequence are taken before fixing an arbitrary cell. Nonresonant and infinite-slope labels eventually fail; finite-label exclusion proves tangent coverage without a cell-dependent extraction. Resetting unused infinite slopes preserves support, and fixed-support rationalization applies without a positive-gain requirement. Conclusion is existence of a rational affine replacement, not equality to the input schedule.
manuscript_review.theorem_6: No quantifier loss found. Theorem 5 transfers arbitrary-schedule existence to affine phases; endpoint capacities then prove the claimed sharp inequality. The responsible residues at q=2d retain both parity classes. The common odd part and fixed finite support are essential hypotheses.
manuscript_review.editorial_issue_sent_to_integrator: Earlier Section 3 sentence excluding arbitrary phase dependence should be qualified after Theorem 5 extends existence on fixed supports. This audit did not edit it.
